The model looks at three key pieces of information. Your age (67) and your monthly income ($14,033) both pull the risk score down, meaning they make you look less likely to miss a payment. However, the amount of revolving credit you are using is very high (about 98% of the limit). That high utilization pushes the risk score up, because it signals that you are close to maxing out your credit lines. When the model balances these influences, it still classifies you as “low risk,” even though the calculated probability of default is 47.8%.
